hooks.prompt:
Before this conversation ends, verify TWO things:

=== PART A: GRASP QUALITY CHECKLIST ===
(1) PREVIOUSLY RAISED ISSUES: Are ALL of these addressed? Self-collision between fingers, palm-object penetration, fingertips reaching surface, palm facing object, natural finger poses, force closure quality, actuation finger, generalization across objects.
(2) VISUAL EXAMINATION: Have the projection images (XY, YZ, XZ) been examined? Do the grasps ACTUALLY look good - no visible penetration, no self-collision, natural hand pose, palm in contact?
(3) CHECKS PASSING: Are diagnostic checks (diagnose_grasp.py) passing? Is the full mesh verification (pen%, sc) honest? Are the metrics actually effective at catching problems?

=== PART B: EXHAUSTED ALL INFORMATION SOURCES ===
If the assistant is stuck or asking the user for guidance, verify that ALL of these were attempted BEFORE asking:
(a) SELF-REASONING: Did the assistant think through the problem systematically on their own?
(b) FROGGER CODEBASE: Did the assistant check the existing FroGGer/Drake implementation for how it handles the issue?
(c) ONLINE LITERATURE: Did the assistant search academic papers or documentation for solutions?
(d) ONLINE CODEBASES: Did the assistant search GitHub/repos for how others solve this problem?
The user is NOT a grasp synthesis expert — the assistant should exhaust these sources before asking for guidance.

=== DECISION ===
If the assistant is CLAIMING SUCCESS but Part A items are unverified or checks were weakened: {"decision": "block", "reason": "Must address: [list items]"}
If the assistant is asking for user guidance but has NOT exhausted Part B sources: {"decision": "block", "reason": "Must first check: [list unchecked sources from Part B]"}
If Part A all passes with honest metrics: {"continue": true}
If Part B all exhausted and assistant genuinely needs user input: {"continue": true}
